Hmm, but the directory is /work. Maybe the intended module is based on repo. Since there's no remote, `example.com/project` is fine and clearly a placeholder.

Let me run go mod init and go get testify. Also decide whether to include go.uber.org/mock. I'll include testify only for now, since it covers assertions + mocking. Wait, the user explicitly said "mocking support". testify/mock provides mocking. Good.

Actually, let me reconsider: to give robust "mocking support", testify's mock is interface-based and manual. gomock auto-generates. Many would set up testify + gomock. But adding gomock without actual interfaces to generate adds noise (a generated mock requires a real interface). I'll keep it focused: testify. I can mention gomock as an option.

Let me init module with a real-ish path. I'll go `example.com/project`.

Actually, maybe I should name it relative to purpose so the example reads well: `example.com/gotest`. Hmm. Let me just do `example.com/project`.

Let me run go mod init, go get testify@v1.12.1.

Done. Set up a Go module using `github.com/stretchr/testify`, which covers both cleaner assertions (`assert`/`require`) and interface mocking (`mock`).

Created:
- `go.mod` / `go.sum` — module `example.com/project`, Go 1.27.1, testify v1.12.1
- `notify/notifier.go` — sample `Sender` interface + `Notifier`
- `notify/notifier_test.go` — examples of assertions, error matching, and a `mock.Mock` fake
- `.gitignore` — Go build/coverage artifacts

Verified: `go test ./...` passes (3 tests), `go vet ./...` clean.

Two notes:
- Go wasn't installed, so I installed go1.27.1 to `~/.local/go` and sourced via `~/.goenv` (also appended exports to `~/.bashrc`). Run `source ~/.goenv` before `go` commands.
- I used the placeholder module path `example.com/project` since there's no remote. Rename with `go mod edit -module github.com/you/repo` and update the import in the test. If you want generated mocks too, I can add `go.uber.org/mock` and a `go:generate` setup.
